note: The depth chart. Depth is the column — 1 through 6; anybody past that is on the squad but in nothing. A name may repeat, both down a column and across one: the same left tackle at three depths is that name three times, and a backup can be second in line at two positions. Offense covers every spot both formations use; defense is the 4-4, our everyday front. Edit this file and rebuild — the page is the file, not a board you rearrange in the browser.

rotations.note: The offense's positional rotations, printed on the depth chart in place of the packages: each a spot and the boys who take it in turn, in order. Every name has to be a boy on the depth chart above, or the build stops.

script_plays.note: The possession script: the plays in the order they are called, down the right of the call sheet. Same rules as package_plays -- an entry is a play's full call and has to name a real play, or the build stops. A play may appear more than once; a script repeats on purpose. Fewer entries than the column has rows is fine, the rest print blank; more than it has rows stops the build, because the column's height is what the rest of the sheet is measured against.

front_slides.note: Where each man of the base eleven goes when we change front. The key is the front's id, then that front's spot, and the value is the 4-4 spot whose player fills it. Every spot in the front must appear exactly once and no 4-4 man twice, or the build stops -- eleven on the field either way. Only fronts that differ from the 4-4 need an entry; the 4-4 is itself.
